description:
Electrical/network general-arrangement sheet titled “CAN D STBD.” This is a CAN-bus topology drawing, not a conventional load-power wiring schematic. It shows no branch-circuit protective devices, breaker/fuse identifiers or ratings, distribution board/row designations, local/panel switches, relay/contactor coils, PLC outputs, terminal strips, connector pin numbers, or individual wire numbers. Accordingly, no printed supply breaker/fuse, power-feed path, or control point can be assigned to any device from this sheet; the CAN lines are communications/status/control-network connections and must not be treated as power feeds. No explicit drawing/sheet continuation cross-reference is visible; title-page references concern document restrictions/export control, not circuit continuation.

CAN topology, traced from the left end when the sheet is viewed upright (image rotated 90° counterclockwise): a “CAN Terminator 120 Ohm” is at the left end of the main CAN D starboard backbone, beside a branch labelled “24V RTN to CAN shield.” The backbone passes serially through CAN Y CONNECTOR drops to SCU, DISPLAY AFT, ESS, EDN STBD, HEP, ECP3, ECP4, and BCP. DISPLAY AFT also connects by a separate CAN Y CONNECTOR branch to ALARM NAV. After BCP, the backbone loops to a central CAN Y CONNECTOR, then continues through another central CAN Y CONNECTOR toward the right-hand section. One central branch runs through an ISOLATOR to a remote CAN Y CONNECTOR with a “CAN Terminator 120 Ohm” and a BL4 drop. The other central branch runs through an ISOLATOR to a remote CAN Y CONNECTOR with a “CAN Terminator 120 Ohm” and a BEL3 drop. The right-hand continuation reaches a CAN Y CONNECTOR with an MC43 drop, then CBS STBD, and ends at “EMS STBD with 120 Ohm” (integral/end termination as printed).

Device characterization is limited to what is printed: SCU, DISPLAY AFT, ALARM NAV, ESS, EDN STBD, HEP, ECP3, ECP4, BCP, BL4, BEL3, MC43, CBS STBD, and EMS STBD are device identifiers/names, but their equipment types (pump, valve, light, controller, sensor, etc.) are not defined on this sheet and are therefore ambiguous. CAN Y CONNECTOR items are network junction/connectors; ISOLATOR items are CAN network isolators; “CAN Terminator 120 Ohm” items are 120-ohm bus terminations. The line topology documents CAN network interconnection only. No separate monitoring/alarm tap is identified except that ALARM NAV is shown as a CAN-connected device branching from DISPLAY AFT’s area of the network; its detailed signal function is not given.

Printed installation note: “NOTE: CAN Shield ground should be kept as short as possible to reduce voltage transients, without extending the CAN backbone.”
